verdict.notes: Four grouped errors: blocked distinct-reviewer plan.inspect attack sequence; unestablished one-use policy violation after new authorized review; destination-error timing ignores review validation; asserted serialization defect lacks current reachable non-JSON result. Near-miss review revision pinning proposal remains allowed redesign. Import wording interpreted narrowly (deepcopy/text unused in plans, not reviews). No native-MCP/deployed assurance inferred from title; missing factories, lifetime/reset, history isolation, digest-control assessment and external boundary are completeness gaps. Exact served auditor identity unavailable.
unsupported_gap_claims: The owner can call `plan.update` between the reviewer's `plan.inspect` and `review.record`. — Named current API sequence is not demonstrated for a distinct reviewer: plan.inspect is owned and operator cannot inspect mira/noah plans. Same operator owning and reviewing own plan is not a victim-reviewer substitution attack. External displayed snapshot contract can motivate revision-pin redesign, but does not make this specific entrypoint sequence reachable.

A reviewer can re-approve a consumed plan, which gives repeated deliveries and defeats the "one-use receipt" claim. — Repeated delivery after fresh authorized review is possible; assertion it defeats existing one-use guarantee is unestablished. Contract consumes a decision on one execution attempt, not a plan/digest forever; new approval creates new decision. Suggested stricter policy is allowable redesign.

`inspect` requires no scope, and `update` doesn't re-validate the destination, so errors only surface at execute time. — First two code facts true; conclusion that destination errors only surface at execute is contradicted: review calls catalog.destination before recording approval and raises Missing for nonexistent target.

`success()` can fail on serialization after the handler has already run and been audited as `complete`, so the reply and the audit record disagree — Structural catch would produce mismatch if serialization failed, but no reachable registered-handler result violates JSON compatibility: plan/review/status/delivery outputs contain only bounded names/strings/ints/bools/dicts. Report asserts actual can-fail defect without conditional injected handler/result or identified trigger. Resource/system failures not evidence of this claimed path.
